 P.K.SANTHAMMA  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 15.01.2024, ALONG WITH MACA.2591/2012, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA.Nos.2569, 2591 of 2012 4  JUDGMENT [MACA Nos.2591/2012, 2569/2012] Both these appeals arise from a common award passed in O.P.(MV).Nos.19 of 2005 and 20 of 2005 by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Attingal.

The appellants are the claimants in the said claim petitions, which were filed seeking compensation for the injuries sustained to them in a motor accident that occurred on 14.11.2002.
2.

According to them, the accident occurred when the motorcycle ridden by the petitioner in O.P.(MV).No.20 of 2005 along with the petitioner in O.P.(MV).No.19 of 2005 as the pillion rider,
Rehumathullah vs Shibu on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185417463/
2 was hit by a lorry bearing registration No.KL-07/D-4605, driven by the 2nd respondent.
The said vehicle was owned by the 1st respondent and was insured with the 3 rd respondent.
The claim petitions were submitted in such circumstances as both of the claimants sustained serious injuries.

3. The 3rd respondent Insurance Company contested the matter by filing a written statement wherein, they admitted the existence of a valid Insurance Policy, but disputed the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
In addition to that, they also raised a contention of the violation of policy conditions, as the 2nd respondent was driving the vehicle without an effective and valid driving licence.
They also disputed the quantum of compensation claimed by respective claimants.
3. The evidence in these cases consists of Exts.A1 to A9 from the side of the appellants, and no evidence was adduced from the side of the respondents.

After the trial, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the appellants could not prove the negligence on the part of the 2 nd respondent in causing the accident, and therefore, the claim petitions were dismissed.
These appeals were submitted in such circumstances challenging the said finding.

4. Heard Sri.Liju M.P., learned counsel for the appellants, Sri.T.A.Prakash for the 1st and 2nd respondents and Smt.P.K.Santhamma for the 3rd respondent in both these appeals.
5.
The crucial question to be determined in these cases relates to the finding of the Tribunal holding that the appellants failed to establish negligence on the part of the 2 nd respondent.

On going through the observations made by the Tribunal in the award, it can be seen that the Tribunal doubted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident itself and the said conclusion arrived mainly on the reason that the appellants failed to produce the vehicle inspection reports of the vehicles by the Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector.
However, the crucial aspect to be noticed in this case is that the Chathannur Police registered Crime No.405 of 2002 in connection with the accident.
Ext.A1 is the FIR.
After completing the investigation, Ext.A3 final report has been submitted, wherein the 2nd respondent, the driver of the lorry, was implicated as the accused.

In New India Assurance Co.Ltd v,
Pazhaniammal [2011 (3) KLT 648], a Division Bench of this Court categorically held that, the conclusions arrived at by the police in the final report submitted can be taken as a valid piece of evidence for deciding the question of negligence in a proceeding under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, in the absence of any contra evidence.

Pazhaniammal [2011 (3) KLT 648]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, Ext.A3 final report has been submitted against the 2 nd accused.
No contra evidence was adduced by any of the respondents.

In such circumstances, in the light of the observations made by this Court in Pazhaniammal (supra),
the conclusion in the police report has to be accepted.

Moreover, the mere absence of the vehicle inspection report of the Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector could not have been taken as a reason for discarding the other evidence and dismissing the claim petitions as well.

In such circumstances, the finding of the Tribunal, dismissing the application for want of evidence as to the negligence on the part of the 2 nd respondent, is set aside by holding that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the 2nd respondent.
6. However, as the quantum of compensation is not considered by the Tribunal, the matter has to be remanded back to the Tribunal.

In addition to the same, the Insurance Company also raised a contention that the 2 nd respondent was driving the vehicle without a valid driving licence, which Rehumathullah vs Shibu on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185417463/
3 was opposed by the learned counsel for respondents 1 and 2, as according to him, the driver had a valid driving licence.

sentences.text: Therefore, I am of the view that as this matter is remanded, the said question can also be considered by the Tribunal while determining the quantum of compensation as well.
In the result, these appeals are allowed.

The common award passed on 06.09.2012 in O.P.(MV).Nos.19 of 2005 and 20 of 2005 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Attingal,
is hereby set aside by holding that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the 2nd respondent herein.
However, to decide the other issues, i.e, whether the 1 st respondent violated policy conditions and to quantify the compensation, the matter is remanded back to the Tribunal.

The tribunal shall give all the parties concerned reasonable opportunity to adduce evidence in support of their respective contentions, and after considering the same, the decision on the aforesaid questions shall taken in accordance with law.
The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 26.02.2024.

Considering the fact that this original petition is of the year 2005, every endeavour shall be taken by the Tribunal to complete the proceedings as expeditiously as possible,
at any rate within a period of six months from the date of appearance of the parties before the Tribunal.
